en: The Apadāna of the Elder Bodhiupaṭṭhāka from the Kuṭajapupphiya Chapter, the Sixth The Apadāna of the Elder Bodhiupaṭṭhāka: In the past, when the Buddha Kassapa was in the world, I was a monk named Upaṭṭhāka, serving the Blessed One. I stood as his attendant for seven days, and with a heart full of joy, I offered him a bodhi tree. Because of that meritorious deed, I have been reborn in heaven, and for a hundred thousand aeons I have enjoyed celestial bliss. Having passed away from there, I have now attained human birth; I am now a forest-dwelling monk, living in the depths of the woods. I have reached the end of suffering and have realized Nibbāna; I have fulfilled my purpose and am free from all defilements. Thus did the Elder Bodhiupaṭṭhāka speak of his own past deeds.
I was a player of the muraja drum;
I was constantly engaged in attending upon [the king].”
Having attended upon me morning and evening,
urged on by the root of my own wholesome merit;
I did not fall into an evil rebirth;
From here I was a lord of people;
a wheel-turning monarch of great power.
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Bodhiupatthaka spoke these verses.
This is the sixth legend of the elder Bodhiupatthaka.
